name: Bartholomew Dias Rounds the Cape of Good Hope
summary: Portuguese explorer Bartolomeu Dias rounds the southernmost tip of Africa, the Cape of Good Hope, proving that the Atlantic and Indian Oceans are connected and that a sea route to India exists. Dias named it "Cape of Storms"; King João II renamed it "Cape of Good Hope" for what it promised. The route enables Vasco da Gama's voyage of 1498.

_quarry.structural_significance: Proves the viability of the sea route to India; enables Portugal's domination of the Indian Ocean trade that begins with da Gama; the route bypasses the Ottoman-controlled eastern Mediterranean, redirecting global trade.
